industry.summary: Belrise sells mainly to two-wheeler makers (82% of FY26 manufacturing revenue). Two-wheeler demand recovered in FY26 after the GST rate cut of late 2025; an analyst on the Q1FY27 call put 2W/3W industry production growth at 20-25% against Belrise's +18%. Over FY16-25 Belrise grew revenue >11.5% a year while domestic 2W industry volumes grew 1.4% a year (company deck, from the prospectus): growth came from content per vehicle and new customers, not the market.
industry.contentPerVehicle: 2W content per vehicle ~Rs12,000 18 months ago, ~Rs20,000 including the two promoter companies being merged (Q4FY26 call); premium-bike chassis worth ~2.2x a commuter chassis (deck).
industry.competition: Sheet-metal, chassis and exhaust supply is fragmented; peers include JBM Auto, Minda Corp, Uno Minda (some products), Endurance (suspension, brakes) and many unlisted vendors. Belrise claims ~24% of Indian 2W metal components (CRISIL, FY24).

excluded.BHARATFORG: Earnings distorted: a Rs358 cr exceptional charge turned the Jun-2026 quarter into a loss, so its ~93x trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 sits on depressed TTM EPS (same exclusion as the other auto-component initiations).
excluded.GABRIEL: No five-year history: Screener's P/E series starts in May-2024 (after Gabriel's restructuring); excluded in every auto-component initiation, kept out here for consistency.

peers.notes: The auto-component peer set of the Uno Minda, Endurance, Motherson and Bosch initiations (same as-of date) with Belrise itself left out. Because Belrise listed in May-2025 and is valued on its own 12-month median, the sector move is the peers' trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026 against their own medians over the same 12 months (Oct-2025 to Sep-2026), as in the Hyundai and Ather initiations; the five-year version is shown too.

brokers.thesis: Raised from Rs250 after Q1FY27: steady quarter, continued order wins, widening footprint (aerospace, renewables). Multiple not in our source; at its May basis (26x FY28E) Rs280 needs FY28E EPS of ~Rs10.8.
Initiation: rising content in passenger and commercial vehicles, support from acquisitions; ~25% upside at initiation.
Post-Q4: multiple raised from 25x; FY27E EPS -2.8%, FY28E +6%; FY26-level margins held through pass-through and OEM negotiations.
Raised from Rs215 after an in-line Q4FY26; earnings to compound; aerospace and defence a new leg.

street.consensus: Centrum (26-May-2026, quoted by Business Today): consensus FY26-28E CAGR revenue 13.0%, EBITDA 15.3%, EPS 27.2%. Stockanalysis showed a ~Rs255 average target (range Rs250-270) in late Jul-2026, before Jefferies' raise.
street.note: We did not find the notes themselves (only press summaries), so the EPS behind each target is implied, not read: Rs250 / 26x = Rs9.6 FY28E for JM and Jefferies (May-2026), on pre-QIP shares and, we believe, including the BAPL/EITSPL merger.

ownership.src: Screener.in shareholding (BSE pattern, Jun-2026 quarter); named promoter stakes from the scheme filing of 31-Jan-2026 (unchanged total 66.45%)
ownership.trend: Promoters 73.01% after the IPO, 66.46% from Dec-2025 (sale), 61.14% after the Jul-2026 QIP (Sep-2026 pattern, filed after our date: we use Jun-2026). FIIs 6.8% → 9.4% and DIIs 7.1% → 10.0% between Jun-2025 and Jun-2026.

governance.board: Founder-led; the MD's wife is a whole-time director and two sons hold senior executive roles (President Strategy, General Manager); majority of the board independent (deck).
governance.pay: MD Rs11.0 cr (+10%, 219x the median employee) and whole-time director Rs4.0 cr in FY26: ~3% of PAT for two family members.
